label: S. 4610

latest_action.text: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 513.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The S. 4610, known as the Pacific POWER Act, directs the U.S. Secretary of State, working with the Secretary of Energy, to promote international cooperation and development of geothermal energy resources, specifically focusing on the Indo-Pacific region. The bill establishes an International Geothermal Program to forge public-private partnerships, advance geothermal technologies, and provide technical and financial assistance to chosen international partners.

affected_groups.effect: Must lead diplomatic engagements, author comprehensive global resource assessments and strategies, establish the International Geothermal Program, and coordinate technical and financial assistance.
affected_groups.group: U.S. Federal Agencies (Department of State, Department of Energy, and others)

affected_groups.effect: Receive targeted U.S. technical assistance, financial tools, research coordination, and support for developing predictable siting, permitting, and regulatory frameworks for geothermal energy.
Gain opportunities to participate in an advisory committee, expand technology and service exports, and enter international public-private partnerships.
affected_groups.group: U.S. Geothermal Industry and Private Sector

key_provisions: Requires the Secretary of State to engage bilaterally and multilaterally on geothermal diplomacy, prioritizing Indo-Pacific allies and partners like Taiwan, the Philippines, Japan, Australia, Indonesia, India, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, and Thailand.

Mandates an initial global assessment report within 180 days to map high-potential geothermal areas, national security interests, and the influence of foreign countries of concern in target energy sectors.
Establishes the International Geothermal Program (IGP) within one year to support public-private partnerships, research, resource exploration, workforce training, and regulatory integration.

Requires the selection of at least five geothermal partner countries—including at least three in the Indo-Pacific, one without commercial geothermal use, and one with expansion potential—to pursue formal agreements.
Directs the creation of a private-sector advisory mechanism involving developers, manufacturers, and nonprofits to advise on technical standards and identify export opportunities.
Outlines implementation requirements, including strategy reports, annual updates to Congress, and coordination of U.S. technical and financial assistance like grants, loans, and loan guarantees.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or direct appropriations limits for fiscal years 2027 through 2031 are not specified in the updated text.
Specific timelines or caps on the total number of personnel to be assigned to the program are not provided.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The S. 4610, known as the Pacific POWER Act, directs the U.S. Secretary of State, working with the Secretary of Energy, to promote international cooperation and development of geothermal energy resources, specifically focusing on the Indo-Pacific region. The bill establishes an International Geothermal Program to forge public-private partnerships, advance geothermal technologies, and provide technical and financial assistance to chosen international partners.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a structured, government-wide framework for U.S. international engagement on clean energy technology. By linking geothermal resource development in strategic foreign regions to national security and economic interests, the legislation seeks to expand markets for U.S. companies while addressing foreign energy vulnerabilities and competition.
